observations.pressure: Customers and staff compete for shelf/checkout throughput while the player crosses the shop floor.
observations.signal: Customer bodies, item stacks, shelves, and checkout stations remain visible in the same frame.
observations.escalation: More actors and stations appear as the shop expands.
observations.failureAttribution: Slow earnings are attributable to a visible logistics bottleneck: stock, travel, or checkout throughput.
observations.recoveryReplay: Return to the nearest depleted shelf/source, restock, then resume checkout.

observations.pressure: Multiple product shelves and upgrade/facility prompts compete for the player's next action.
observations.signal: Item-specific shelf icons, carried stacks, coin amounts, and construction prompts are visible at world locations.
observations.escalation: New facilities and denser customer traffic raise travel and replenishment demand.
observations.failureAttribution: The player can see which shelf or route is causing the delay rather than reading a hidden meter.
observations.recoveryReplay: Local restock and staff/facility actions restore the same loop without resetting the scene.

observations.pressure: A hired employee can visibly enter a sleep/slacking state, and a separate animal/auxiliary role can also present a wake-up task while the store remains active.
observations.signal: WAKE UP THE EMPLOYEE / WAKE UP THE ANIMAL banners, a green down arrow, sleeping-face bubble and Z marker are shown in world space.
observations.escalation: The reminder coexists with MAX production, cash thresholds, customer traffic and timed ad offers, so recovery competes with normal operations.
observations.failureAttribution: The visible sleep cue identifies a non-working helper as a local automation bottleneck; the recording does not prove why it happened or how it is cleared.
observations.recoveryReplay: The same scene continues without reset; exact wake interaction and whether productivity resumes immediately remain unknown.

observations.pressure: The shop stays active during upgrade/construction interactions.
observations.signal: Currency changes, upgrade state, and customer demand are shown together.
observations.escalation: The world becomes busier while the next actionable station remains visually findable.
observations.failureAttribution: Progress or stall is explained by visible inventory, queue, and facility state.
observations.recoveryReplay: After the transaction, the player immediately returns to source→shelf→customer→checkout.

transferablePatterns: Use world-space state cues and item-specific silhouettes so pressure is readable without long helper text.
Keep the source→inventory→customer→checkout loop active during upgrades.
Make construction/payment a short visible transition followed by a persistent functional world object.
Preserve local recovery: restock the bottleneck and replay the same loop.
rejectCopying: Do not copy Monkey Mart names, banana content, characters, assets, map geometry, UI arrangement, prompts, or tuning values.
Apply only generic logistics/automation principles to the original sea-otter beach seafood expression.
unknowns: Exact internal economy and unlock thresholds are not inferable from the recording and must not be copied.
Platform-specific behavior is not evidenced by this desktop recording.
